Subject: Logging & Redaction Controls — Post-call recap and next steps

Hi Alice / Samir —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can align on the technical controls FinTechCo needs for PII and sensitive data handling.

Call recap (high level):
- You are most worried about request/response logs containing PII (names, account numbers, payment tokens) and trace IDs that could be used to correlate to internal systems.
- Primary asks: configurable request/response redaction, header masking (authorization/trace headers), retention policy controls per environment, and confirmation of data residency for logs stored in prod.
- Risk tolerance: must be able to demonstrate masking/redaction for SOC and audit requests; default logs can contain metadata only.

What Redwood can provide (summary):
- Request/response redaction: configurable regex and JSON-path based masking at the runtime level. Option to redact full request/response body or only configured keys.
- Header masking: support for masking/stripping headers (Authorization, Cookie, X-Trace-Id) before logs are persisted.
- Trace IDs: we can either anonymize trace IDs in persisted logs or map them to ephemeral IDs stored in a separate protected store with KMS encryption.
- Retention controls: per-customer retention TTLs with configurable retention windows (30/90/365 days) and auto-deletion workflows; exportable audit logs for compliance.
- Data residency: logs written to region-specific object storage (US east/west/EU) based on customer config; private deployments can keep logs entirely on-prem.

Attachments: I attached a short overview of our logging controls (redwood-logging-controls-overview.pdf) and a draft SLA with retention language (SLA-draft-FinTechCo.docx).

Next steps (proposed):
1) Neha to provide a short technical note with example config snippets for redaction + header masking (by Wed 26 Aug).
2) FinTechCo to confirm whether you need trace-ID persisting or ephemeral-only (Samir / Alice).
3) If acceptable, we’ll put together a sealed carve-out in the draft SLA for log residency and retention and share a redline.
4) Quick follow-up call next week to review the config and any PoC scope (30 min).

Thanks — happy to sync or change priorities based on what you need most.

Best,

Hi Marissa / Neha / Dylan —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Trace IDs: we prefer trace IDs not be present in any persisted logs by default. If there is a strong operational need to persist them, they must be pseudonymized and stored in a separate encrypted store with strict access controls.
2) Retention: default production logs must be 90 days, with the ability to set 30/365 for specific environments. We will need an exportable chain-of-custody for deletions for audits.
3) Redaction: we need both key-based redaction (JSON keys) and pattern-based (credit card regex). Can you provide example configs and sample logs (before/after redaction) so our security team can review?

Samir and I are available for the follow-up call next Wed afternoon.

Thank you —
Alice Johnson
Security Engineering Manager | FinTechCo

Hi Alice / Samir —

Quick technical note and example configs as requested. See examples inline below (sample snippets only). I can share sanitized before/after redaction samples in the follow-up.

1) Key-based JSON redaction (runtime config):
- config: {"redact_keys": ["ssn","account_number","card_number"], "mode": "mask"} -> replaces values with <REDACTED>.

2) Pattern-based redaction (regex):
- pattern: credit card regex -> replace with <CARD_REDACTED>.

3) Header masking example: strip_headers: ["Authorization","Cookie","X-Trace-Id" ]

4) Trace ID handling options:
- ephemeral-only: runtime generates per-request trace, not persisted.
- pseudonymized: map original trace to a KMS-encrypted GUID stored in separate logs-store with limited IAM access (audit logs show access).

5) Retention: TTL policy per-customer bucket; deletion is executed via automated job and emits an audit record (signed timestamp + operator) we can export on request.

Action items from my side:
- I will prepare a small sanitized log sample (before/after) and an example runtime config file by EOD Wed (26 Aug).
- If you want, I can also include a short runbook for our SOC showing how to request deletes / export audit trail.

Let me know if you need the pseudonymization design doc ahead of the call.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
